transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Well, honestly, what finally pushed me to come in is just how tense I am all the time. My shoulders and my neck, they just stay clenched all day long. It's like I'm constantly bracing for a classroom observation that never ends. And by the time evening rolls around, my jaw aches so badly I can hardly even enjoy playing my guitar anymore. I just need to figure out how to stop feeling so physically wound up.
When you notice your shoulders and neck getting tense during the day, do you also find yourself worrying about things, or is it mainly just the physical tension without much worry in your mind?

No, it's definitely not just the physical tension. My mind is going constantly. It's like I can't stop worrying. I just keep circling back to things... like whether I'll ever get hired again, or if I've completely ruined my reputation with the parents. I worry that my retirement is slipping away. It even gets down to the small things, like if I make a tiny mistake during a story-time activity, my mind jumps to thinking that maybe I shouldn't even be trusted with children anymore. So, yeah, the worry is definitely there with the tension.
How long have you been experiencing this constant worry and tension? Has it been going on for several months, or did it start more recently?

It's been... well, definitely more than a few months. It's been going on for about a year and two months now. That's, um... that's when I was fired from the preschool. It pretty much all started right after that.

Besides the worries about your job and reputation, do you find yourself worrying excessively about other areas of your life — like your health, your family relationships, or everyday situations — even when there's no particular reason to be concerned?

No, not really. I mean, my health is fine, and I don't really stress about my family or relationships. It's... it's pretty much entirely focused on the job situation and my finances. I don't really find myself panicking over other everyday things unless it connects back to my career or my future. So, no, I haven't really noticed it bleeding into those other areas.
Before you were fired from the preschool about 14 months ago, did you experience periods of excessive worry or physical tension like this, or did it really start after that job loss?

No, I never really had this problem before. I mean, I'd get stressed sometimes, sure, but not like this. The constant worrying and the tension in my shoulders... that all started after I lost my job. Before that, I felt pretty normal.

When you're not thinking about your job situation or finances — like when you're playing guitar or doing something else that takes your focus — does the worry and tension tend to go away, or does it stay with you regardless of what you're doing?

It... it pretty much stays with me. I try to get my mind off it, I really do. I'll tell myself to just sit down and make a list, or pray, or go outside and weed the garden—just try to focus on the next practical step. But it doesn't really work. One worry just hands off to another, and... well, next thing I know, I've lost half the afternoon to it.

Looking back over this past year since you lost your job, have there been any periods — even a week or two — where the constant worry and tension significantly lessened or went away, or has it been pretty much continuous the whole time?

No, it's been pretty much continuous. I mean, there hasn't really been a break. It's just been this constant weight... this constant worrying the whole time. I haven't had a week or even a few days where I felt like it went away. It's just always there.

Before you lost your job, even going back years, did you ever have periods where you felt persistently worried or anxious about things, or times when you felt physically tense or on edge for extended periods?

No, not really. I mean, like I said, I'd get stressed out like anyone else would, but it never lasted for days or weeks. I never had this... this feeling of being on edge all the time before I lost my job. It really did just start after that happened.

When the worry and tension happen during the day, can you usually trace it back to something specific — like thinking about a job application, or seeing something that reminds you of the preschool — or does it sometimes just hit you out of nowhere without any clear trigger?

I'm not really sure, to be honest. I haven't exactly noticed a strict pattern with it. 

I mean, sometimes I know it's because I was looking at a job board or thinking about my old classroom, but... other times, I really couldn't tell you what started it. It just sort of happens, and I'll suddenly realize my chest is tight and my mind is racing. I just haven't really kept track of exactly what triggers it every time.

If you were to imagine that you got hired back at a preschool or found a stable new job tomorrow, do you think the constant worry and tension would go away, or do you think it would still be there even with that resolved?

I honestly don't know. I mean... I'd like to think that if I got hired somewhere tomorrow, it would all just stop and I'd feel normal again. But I'm really not sure anymore. 

The worry is just so heavy right now, I don't know if a new job would actually make it all go away, or if my mind would just stay stuck like this. I just really couldn't tell you for sure.

If we could somehow completely resolve the job situation — say you got hired back or found a new stable job and felt secure about your finances — do you think your worry and tension would gradually go away over time, or do you worry that your mind might stay stuck in this anxious state even after the job problem was solved?

I... I think I just answered that. I really don't know. I'd hope it would go away, but I can't say for sure if my mind would just stay like this. I haven't really thought about it that way, to be honest.

Since you lost your job 14 months ago, have you noticed whether your worry tends to get worse on days when you're actively job searching or thinking about the preschool situation, compared to days when you're not focused on those things?

I haven't really compared the days, to be honest. It just... it feels like the tension is pretty much always there in the background. Whether I'm sitting at the computer sending out resumes or just trying to do things around the house, my mind is still going. So, no, I haven't really noticed if actively searching makes it worse than when I'm not doing those things. The worry just feels pretty constant either way.

Looking back, do you think most people in your situation — someone who lost their job and was worried about their reputation — would still be feeling this level of constant worry and physical tension after 14 months, or do you think your reaction has been more intense than what would be typical?

I honestly don't know what's typical. I mean, I guess anyone would be upset about losing their job and their reputation, but... I don't really know if they'd still be feeling this wound up and tense after more than a year. I haven't really talked to anyone else who's been through this exact thing, so I couldn't say if my reaction is more intense or not. It's just what I've been dealing with.

When you think about your job loss and finances now, compared to when it first happened 14 months ago, do those specific worries feel just as intense and urgent as they did back then, or have they actually gotten somewhat less intense even though the worry and tension overall haven't gone away?

I'm not really sure if the specific worries about the job and money are less intense now. It's hard to separate it out. I mean, the whole situation still feels pretty overwhelming, and I'm still tense all the time. I guess I haven't really stopped to measure if the urgency of those exact thoughts has changed since the beginning. It just all kind of blends together into this constant feeling of being on edge.
